findings.problem: The hshape case analysis that gives 0 < A b and s b ∈ Icc 0 1 is written twice in this proof, with the same rcases each time. The same two blocks are copied into ControlledCollarLoop.lean (lines 88-95) and JetVelocityLoop.lean (lines 114-121). That makes six copies in all, differing only in how the point is named. The reasoning is nontrivial: it uses arctan positivity and 2·arctan a ≤ A in the base case, and π < A together with s = 1 in the interior case. It depends only on the a, A, s part of the disjunction, not on c.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma next to reparametrized_two_turns in BlendedReparamTurns.lean:

lemma shape_pos_mem_Icc {a A s : ℝ} {q r : Prop}
    (h : (0 < a ∧ 2 * Real.arctan a ≤ A ∧ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ q) ∨ (s = 1 ∧ Real.pi < A ∧ r)) :
    0 < A ∧ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1

Proof sketch: rcases h. In the left case, A > 0 from mul_pos two_pos (Real.arctan_pos.mpr h.1) combined with h.2.1, and s ∈ Icc from h.2.2.1. In the right case, A > 0 from Real.pi_pos.trans h.2.1, and s ∈ Icc after rw [h.1] using ⟨zero_le_one, le_rfl⟩. The abstract Props q and r let the lemma fit every file's c-condition.

Rewritten use in the target (the third bullet):
  · intro b hb θ hθ
    obtain ⟨hAb, hsb⟩ := shape_pos_mem_Icc (hshape b (hKL hb))
    exact reparametrized_two_turns ha hA hs hh hW hρ hpos (fun b _ => hper b) hmass (hKW (hKL hb)) (hapos b hb) hAb hsb hθ

In ControlledCollarLoop the call is shape_pos_mem_Icc (hshape b ⟨hKL hb, hnotU b hb⟩). In JetVelocityLoop it is shape_pos_mem_Icc (hshape _ ⟨hKL hx, hnotU⟩). In both, the final reparametrized_two_turns / simpa call is unchanged.
findings.benefit: Three files lose about 8 lines each and the double rcases. The case analysis is proved once, in the file that already holds the two-turn criterion. If the hshape form changes, only one proof needs updating.

findings.problem: The same three-part assembly appears in this proof, in ControlledCollarLoop.lean and in JetVelocityLoop.lean. It takes the density facts (hW, hρ, hpos, hper, hmass, hmean) and produces three conclusions about the reparametrized blended loop: smoothness of the angle (hα), periodicity of the angle (the reparametrize_periodic bullet) and the vector mean (hqmean, from reparametrize_mean followed by .trans hmean). The target and ControlledCollarLoop contain textually identical hα, hp and hqmean blocks and identical periodicity bullets. JetVelocityLoop does the same with the points renamed to j and with H = h ∘ fst. Each copy has to restate the long integral expression of hqmean and wire the same five hypotheses (hW hρ hpos (fun b _ => hper b) hmass) into three different PositiveDensity lemmas.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma beside reparametrized_two_turns, generic over B with the instances used in BlendedReparamTurns.lean:

lemma reparametrized_blended_loop {a A s h : B → ℝ} {c : B → LoopDensity.Plane}
    (ha : ContDiff ℝ ∞ a) (hA : ContDiff ℝ ∞ A) (hs : ContDiff ℝ ∞ s) (hh : ContDiff ℝ ∞ h)
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hρ : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ ρ (U ×ˢ univ))
    (hpos : ∀ b ∈ U, ∀ t, 0 < ρ (b, t)) (hper : ∀ b ∈ U, Function.Periodic (fun t => ρ (b, t)) 1)
    (hmass : ∀ b ∈ U, (∫ t in 0..1, ρ (b, t)) = 1)
    (hmean : ∀ b ∈ U, (∫ t in 0..1, ρ (b, t) • blendedPath (a b) (A b) (s b) (h b) t) = c b) :
    ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (PositiveDensity.reparametrize ρ (fun z => unitAngle (a z.1) (A z.1) (s z.1) (h z.1) z.2)) (U ×ˢ univ) ∧
    (∀ b ∈ U, Function.Periodic (fun t => PositiveDensity.reparametrize ρ (fun z => unitAngle (a z.1) (A z.1) (s z.1) (h z.1) z.2) (b, t)) 1) ∧
    ∀ b ∈ U, (∫ t in 0..1, PositiveDensity.reparametrize ρ (fun z => blendedPath (a z.1) (A z.1) (s z.1) (h z.1) z.2) (b, t)) = c b

Proof sketch: refine ⟨reparametrize_smoothOn hU hρ hpos hper' hmass (unitAngle_smooth ha hA hs hh).contDiffOn, fun b hb => reparametrize_periodic hU hρ hpos hper' hmass (fun b _ => unitAngle_periodic (a b) (A b) (s b) (h b)) hb, fun b hb => (reparametrize_mean hU hρ hpos hper' hmass (blendedPath_smooth ha hA hs hh).contDiffOn hb).trans (hmean b hb)⟩. Here hper' is fun b _ => hper b. The lemma is stated for the ∀ b ∈ U periodicity hypothesis; unitAngle_periodic would have to move into BlendedReparamTurns.lean, or the lemma into this file's namespace.

Rewritten use in the target: after obtaining hρ … hmean, write obtain ⟨hα, hperα, hqmean⟩ := reparametrized_blended_loop ha hA hs hh hW hρ hpos hper hmass hmean, then refine ⟨h, hh, hhc, hhs, …, hρ, hpos, hper, hmass, hα, hperα, hqmean, ?_, ?_⟩. This deletes hp, hqmean and the two one-line bullets. ControlledCollarLoop uses the identical call, with hmean derived from LoopDensity.mass_and_mean as it already does. JetVelocityLoop calls it with H in place of h and hmean := fun j hj => (hboth j hj).2.

This lemma should be combined with the first finding. The two-turns and large-turns calls stay as they are.
findings.benefit: Each of the three loop-assembly proofs shrinks by about 12 lines. The long integral statement and the five-argument wiring of three PositiveDensity lemmas live in one place. The target becomes a short sequence: pick W and δ, pick h, apply the lemma, discharge the two-turn and large-turn goals. A fix to the reparametrization API needs one edit instead of three.
